items.t: Declared legal victory after the South Carolina Supreme Court upheld the 2023 Fetal Heartbeat and Protection from Abortion Act against Planned Parenthood's legal challenge.
items.q: South Carolina Attorney General Alan Wilson today declared legal victory following the South Carolina Supreme Court’s decision to uphold the state’s 2023 Fetal Heartbeat and Protection from Abortion Act.

items.t: Supports a DHHS rule that would undo the Biden-era Section 504 Rule defining gender dysphoria as a covered disability.
items.q: Attorney General Alan Wilson is supporting a DHHS rule that would undo the Biden-era Section 504 Rule defining “gender dysphoria” as a covered disability.

items.t: Said the Biden-era Section 504 rule contradicted federal law and common sense.
items.q: “This Biden-era rule contradicted federal law and common sense,” Attorney General Wilson stated.

items.t: Said the sole intention of the lawsuit was to remove gender identity disorders from Section 504 and restore it to what Congress originally passed.
items.q: Our sole intention in the original lawsuit was to remove gender identity disorders and restore Section 504 to what Congress passed originally, so our work is done here.

record.t: Announced his candidacy for governor on June 23, 2025.
record.q: South Carolina Attorney General Alan Wilson announced his candidacy for governor on Monday, June 23, 2025, accompanied by his family.

record.t: Was elected South Carolina's 51st Attorney General in 2010 and re-elected in 2014, 2018 and 2022.
record.q: Alan Wilson was elected South Carolina’s 51st Attorney General on November 2, 2010, re-elected to a second term on November 4, 2014, re-elected to a third term on November 6, 2018, and re-elected to a fourth term on November 8, 2022.

record.office: Assistant Attorney General of South Carolina
record.t: Served as a prosecution division intern under Charlie Condon and as an Assistant Attorney General under Henry McMaster.
record.q: Previously, he served as a prosecution division intern under Charlie Condon and as an Assistant Attorney General under Henry McMaster.

record.t: Challenged the Biden-era Section 504 Rule in federal court and announced South Carolina is pulling out of the lawsuit.
record.q: My Office challenged that rule in federal court. Now that President Trump is in office, his administration is working to undue the challenged rule, which I support. As a result, South Carolina is pulling out of the lawsuit.

record.t: Announced the arrest of Michael Glean Williams, 70, on two charges connected to the sexual exploitation of a minor.
record.q: Attorney General Alan Wilson announced the arrest of Michael Glean Williams, 70, on two charges connected to the sexual exploitation of a minor.

record.t: Said in a January 13 letter to Rep. Nancy Mace that complying with her records request would delay hundreds of cases.
record.q: Wilson's January 13th letter to Rep. Mace stated: "Spending so much time on your request would cause hundreds of cases to be delayed and would effectively shut down the Office's Internet Crimes Against Children and Special Prosecution sections for months.

record.t: Won the Republican nomination for governor of South Carolina, defeating Lt. Gov. Pamela Evette in the runoff.
record.q: The candidate Trump endorsed, state Attorney General Alan Wilson, defeated Lt. Gov. Pamela Evette in a landslide on Tuesday to capture the GOP nomination in the race to succeed term-limited Republican Gov. Henry McMaster.
